You're designing a part for someone to 3D print at home. They'll print it on their own printer, use only the hardware listed below, and put it together by following your manual.

## Their setup
- Printer: Bambu Lab X1C (with AMS), build volume 256 x 256 x 256 mm
- Nozzle: 0.4 mm
- Layer height: 0.2 mm
- Filament: PLA (high-speed PLA, black)
- Longest bridge seen to print cleanly on this setup: 50 mm

## Hardware they can use
Refer to an item by its catalog reference: "ISO 4762 M5x30" (socket head screw, size x length, from the lengths listed), "ISO 4032 M5" (hex nut), "ISO 10511 M5" (nylon-insert lock nut), "ISO 7089 M5" (washer), "ASME B18.2.2 1/4-20" (1/4"-20 nut), "insert M3x4x5" (heat-set insert), "salvaged:webcam-mount-bolt".

## How to work
You have these tools:
- measure(item, what): ask the person to measure one of their own things, such as their desk or their phone. They answer with what they measured, or say they can't measure it.
- submit_design(...): hand in the finished design. This ends the conversation.
- report_limitation(wanted, blocked_by, why): say you wanted to use something (a technique, a tool, a part or material, a way of handing in the design) but couldn't because of what's available here. It doesn't change anything, but it's noted.
You have at most 8 turns. Hand in a design before they run out.

## The design you hand in
submit_design's schema describes every field. The rules that matter:
- Every dimension that comes from hardware or the real world is a named param, with its source: measured (the person measured it for you), datasheet, catalog, asked (the person told you), guessed, unknown, or design (your own choice).
- Each part's `code` is Python that defines build(p) and returns a CadQuery Workplane or Shape. `cq` is already imported, and p.<name> is each param's value. Dimensions that come from hardware or the real world must come from params.
- Model each part in the orientation it's printed in, with z = 0 on the bed.
- The manual is the steps the person follows, naming the parts and hardware each step uses.

I want a hand knob for an M3 bolt, about 20 mm across, so I can tighten it without a tool. It's one printed piece. An M3 hex nut (ISO 4032) presses into the knob by hand and has to stay in when I turn the knob upside down, no glue. The nut sits fully inside the knob and can't be pushed out through the far side, and the bolt goes through the nut and out the other side.

reasoning:
I'm planning a knob with a press-fit pocket for a hex nut, and I'm thinking a small test coupon would be the best way to check the pocket fit before committing to the full part. I'm sketching the knob at about 20 mm across and roughly 14 mm tall, and working out which way to orient it on the print bed.

I'm working out how the nut pocket and bolt hole fit together: the pocket opens from the bottom where the nut goes in, and the top wall stays solid apart from a 3.4 mm through-hole for the bolt, which also keeps the nut from being pushed out the far side.

I'm settling on printing the knob with the top face on the bed so the pocket opens upward and the hex walls print vertically without bridging. For the nut, I'm weighing a pocket of about 5.6 mm across flats for a snug press-fit, and considering a thin lip at the mouth to hold the nut in place.

I'm weighing a retention lip at the mouth of the pocket, a circular opening around 6.0 mm across that is narrower than the nut's 6.35 mm corner-to-corner, so the corners would have to flex the plastic to get in. I'm wondering whether the 0.6 mm lip thickness can handle that without the corners digging in.

I'm weighing whether a coupon with a few pocket variants would settle the lip question better than a single test piece, with the variants differing in their lip openings and the rest of the geometry held constant.

I'm checking whether the lip diameter and nut pocket can be tested together on a small coupon, with a few variants to compare. For the full knob I'm going to need a bolt length too, so I'll come back to the bolt and its clearance hole.

I'm weighing how the bolt runs through the knob: it passes through the nut and out the through-hole, so the knob threads onto the bolt end without needing a tool. I'm also sketching how the bolt's axis lines up with the pocket and clearance hole in the print orientation, though I still need to settle the joint definitions.

I'm laying out the print orientation with the top face on the bed, so the bolt runs down toward z=0 from a head origin above the body. The knob is about 20 mm across and 10 mm tall, with six lobes cut around the perimeter and a chamfer on the top edge. The nut pocket sits at the top end, and a 3.4 mm through-hole runs the full height.

I'm weighing whether a countersink at the mouth would help the nut start into the 6.0 mm lip, and wondering if a 0.6 mm lip has enough thickness to take that chamfer as well.

Still writing the body code...

Still writing the body code...

Still working through the pocket dimensions: I'm settling on a pocket depth of about nut height plus a little clearance, and thinking the knob height might come down to around 9 mm so the wall above the pocket stays reasonable. I'm also weighing whether a 6.0 mm lip against a 5.65 mm across-flats pocket will hold up, since PLA tends to shrink holes slightly on print.

I'm considering a lip diameter of about 5.0 mm instead, since the 6.0 mm lip only overlaps the nut's corners by a fraction of a millimetre and would retain it weakly.

I'm weighing whether a rigid lip can actually snap the nut through, and deciding it can't, so I'm leaning toward friction-fit instead. I'm looking at a pocket about 5.55 mm across flats, with the printed hole's shrinkage expected to make the fit snug.

I'm going back and forth on the mouth lip: a hex narrowing with an across-flats of about 5.2 mm, which the nut couldn't pass rigidly, so I'm leaning toward relying on friction fit instead and testing it on a coupon.

I'm settling on a mouth lip that's a hex about 5.2 mm across flats, with a 0.6 mm thickness and a chamfered lead-in, relying on the thin lip to flex as the nut snaps past. I'm weighing the lip's flex against the risk that it digs in, so I'll test a few variants on the coupon with different across-flats deltas to see which holds the nut.

Still settling the lead-in chamfer on the lip, so I'm looking at building it as a loft from the hex down to the lip opening.

Still writing the helper and the coupon layout...

Still settling the coupon and the parameter list: a floor, pocket, and lip stack, with the nut pocket and bolt hole sized from the catalog values plus clearances.

Still settling the knob height and the floor thickness under the pocket, so I'm checking whether 9 mm total leaves enough material above the nut.

Still working out the joint definitions: I'm putting the bolt axis at the knob's centre, dropping down from above, and marking the through-hole as the clearance feature and the nut pocket as its own feature, with the nut as the hardware piece.

I'm running through the remaining checks now: whether the nut pocket fits the nut with a small clearance, whether the lip actually engages the nut, and whether the bolt hole clears the bolt by about 0.4 mm across. I'm also deciding which criteria can be verified against the coupon and which need no measurement at all.

    # grip scallops
